message.reasoning:
I am deciding how to handle my turn in jail.

I have two get-out-of-jail-free cards and $818 cash. The opponent has $395 and owns red properties with three to four houses, plus Boardwalk unmortgaged. I will stay in jail.

Leaving jail would risk landing on the opponent's reds and feeding them houses to complete their monopoly. I have four houses on each orange and three to four on each pink. Hoteling would return four houses to the bank for the opponent to buy. I am currently on Vermont Avenue.

The opponent landed on my mortgaged Vermont Avenue and paid nothing. I am checking the board positions to plan their next move.

The opponent's next roll from Vermont could land them on St Charles, States, Virginia, St James, Tennessee, or New York. These are all my pink and orange properties with three to four houses. The rent would be significant.

From Vermont, 21 of 36 possible rolls hit my properties. The opponent has only $395 cash.

The opponent would face $450 in rent from St Charles, States, or Virginia with three houses. They would face $700 or $750 from St James, Tennessee, or New York with four houses. With only $395 cash, they would have to sell properties to pay.

I am checking the rent on the red properties. Kentucky with three houses pays $700. Indiana with three houses pays $700. Illinois with four houses pays $925. I want the opponent to hit these expensive reds while I stay safely in jail collecting rent.

I am rechecking the rent on the red properties. My notes list Illinois at $1100, but standard Monopoly rules show four houses there pay $925 and a hotel pays $1100. I need to verify which table applies.

The orange property rent values match standard four-house rates. The Illinois rent figures I previously recorded were actually hotel values, not four-house rates. Four houses on Illinois pay $925.

I can barely afford the $700 rent from Kentucky or Indiana with three houses. Illinois four-house rent is $925, which I cannot pay without selling properties or mortgaging. Leaving jail would risk landing on those expensive reds.

I will roll for doubles. I have already spent one turn in jail and can attempt again.
